idiom_name: N worker goroutines ranging over one shared channel (fan-out) with WaitGroup shutdown
implementation_notes: A receive from a Go channel is atomic: when several goroutines range over the same channel, each element is delivered to exactly one of them, so fan-out - `for i := 0; i < n; i++ { go worker(jobs) }` - is the entire competing-consumer pool and no dispatcher exists. Closing the jobs channel is the end-of-stream marker; sync.WaitGroup (or golang.org/x/sync/errgroup for error propagation and cancellation) waits for in-flight work. Cross-process or durable work replaces the channel with a broker client (SQS, Kafka, NATS queue groups) around which the same N goroutines loop.
pitfalls: Iterating with `for j := range jobs` without ever closing the channel blocks every worker forever; close exactly once, from the producer side.
A panic in one worker terminates the whole process - there is no supervisor; recover inside the goroutine or isolate the work in a subprocess when a bad message must not take the pool down.
Spawning a goroutine per message instead of a fixed pool reintroduces unbounded concurrency and loses the channel's backpressure.
